The answer is **A**: glycolysis nets 2 ATP from glucose and 3 ATP from glycogen by substrate-level phosphorylation. Glucose yields 4 ATP and costs 2 in the investment phase. Glycogen is cleaved by phosphorylase to glucose-1-phosphate, which skips the hexokinase ATP cost, so it nets 3. The team note's two options (3 from glucose) don't match standard biochemistry, so I'm not changing my answer.
